# Fairpractice Recoupments (`fairpractice-recoupments`)

Matches payer recoupments and offsets to the original claims: the same claim taken back twice, more taken than was paid, takebacks beyond the lookback you set, recoupments with no notice on file, takebacks for claims you cannot find, and appeal windows still open. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Recoupments never files appeals or disputes. Fairpractice Recoupments never sends refunds.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Money recovery and practice finance · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-recoupments demo
npx -y fairpractice-recoupments mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up practice, patients and payers. Any likeness to real people is chance. The 18-month lookback and 120-day appeal window are examples, not any state's law or payer's rule.

- [`recoupments.csv`](fixtures/recoupments.csv), [`paid-claims.csv`](fixtures/paid-claims.csv) and [`notices.csv`](fixtures/notices.csv). Planted (as of November 15, 2026):
  - CL-202: taken back on September 1 and again on October 15. The first takeback's appeal window closes November 29.
  - CL-203: 220 taken back on a claim paid 180.
  - CL-204: paid December 2024, recouped October 2026, beyond the 18-month lookback.
  - CL-205: recouped November 2 with no notice on file.
  - CL-999: a takeback for a claim not in your paid claims.
  - CL-207: appeal window (120 days from the July 20 notice) closes November 17.
  - CL-201: recouped with notice; appeal open until January 13.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 120 days to appeal, 21-day warning, 18-month lookback. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `recoup_check` | List duplicate takebacks, excess takebacks, late recoupments, missing notices, unmatched takebacks and open appeal windows. | runs |
| `recoup_write_report` | Write recoupments.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and recoupments.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/recoup). | runs |
| `recoup_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `recoup_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `recoup_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `recoup_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `appeal_submit` | Fairpractice Recoupments never files appeals or disputes. | refused |
| `refund_send` | Fairpractice Recoupments never sends refunds. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `recoup_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `recoupments` (required) | Recoupment or offset lines under --root (from remits or payer letters): payer, date, original claim reference, amount, reason, check or EFT number |
| `claims` (required) | Your paid claims: claim number, patient, payer, date of service, paid amount, paid date |
| `notices` | Optional overpayment notices received: payer, claim reference, notice date, amount |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: appeal_days, warn_days, lookback_months, notice_lead_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-recoupments inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Recoupments (`recoupments`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `remit_date` (required) | date | Remit Date, Date, Check Date, EFT Date, Offset Date, Payment Date |
| `claim_ref` (required) | text | Claim #, Claim Ref, Original Claim, Claim ID, Patient Control #, ICN, Reference |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Recoupment, Offset, Takeback, Adjustment Amount, Amt |
| `reason` | text | Reason, Reason Code, PLB Code, Adjustment Reason |
| `check` | text | Check #, Check, EFT #, Trace # |

### Paid claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` (required) | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, Claim Number, Encounter, Encounter ID, Visit ID, Invoice |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `dos` | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Insurance Paid, Amount Paid, Allowed Paid |
| `paid_date` | date | Paid Date, Payment Date, Remit Date, Check Date |

### Overpayment notices (`notices`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `claim_ref` (required) | text | Claim #, Claim Ref, Original Claim, Claim ID, Patient Control #, ICN, Reference |
| `notice_date` (required) | date | Notice Date, Letter Date, Date, Received |
| `amount` | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |

## Settings file (`recoup_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `appeal_days` | Days to appeal from the notice (or the recoupment if no notice), by payer name, plus "default" (default 120). Set from your contracts. |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn about an appeal window closing; default 21 |
| `lookback_months` | Months after payment beyond which a recoupment is flagged (your state limit or contract); off when not set |
| `notice_lead_days` | Days of notice required before a recoupment; default 0 (any notice before it) |

## Memory

`recoup_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `recoup_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-recoupments": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-recoupments",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-recoupments -- npx -y fairpractice-recoupments mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-recoupments tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-recoupments sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-recoupments inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-recoupments call recoup_check '{"recoupments":"<recoupments>","claims":"<claims>"}'
fairpractice-recoupments eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-recoupments demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
